correctness.rationale: Graph vertices and incidence are explicit over the field of three elements. Elementary distance formulas reconstruct all pairwise graph distances; the proof excludes every <4 case and all wrong four-landmark splits, derives four necessary geometric conditions, proves them sufficient, and counts \(27\cdot2\cdot2\cdot2=216\). The standalone source verifies pair-separation predicates independently of the finite-field distance-signature predicate for each of \(2^{18}\) subsets, matches the geometric criterion on all \(\binom{18}{4}=3060\) candidates, and checks 216 explicit automorphisms and two 108-set orbits. The full polynomial sums to 243834 and no unstated asymptotic generalization is made.

value.rationale: A distance-landmark problem on the classical smallest biaffine incidence net has previously been given as a minimum metric dimension of four. Its complete optimal-set geometric criterion and exact count 216 provide a usable construction/obstruction theory, while the polynomial determines the entire feasible-set size distribution; the two inequivalent symmetry classes highlight nontrivial geometric variation within optimal placements. None of that information follows from knowing only the minimum size, and the natural object and invariant are motivated independently of arbitrary parameter choices.
